newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Gulf Air Airbus pilot hurt as he aborts takeoff.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air Airbus pilot hurt as he aborts takeoff.

text.p: The pilot and several other people aboard a Gulf Air Airbus were injured on Monday when he aborted a takeoff at Abu Dhabi airport, the airline said.

The front wheel came off the A-320, which was on a flight to Cairo via Bahrain, sending the nose skidding along the runway, the civil aviation authority said. The 107 passengers and eight crew were evacuated.
"It is not clear at this point what is the reason for aborting the takeoff," Gulf Air said in a statement after the accident around 1100 am (0700 GMT).
The pilot sustained the most serious injury and was in stable condition in hospital. Hospital sources said he was British.
Some 13 other people were lightly injured as they slid down chutes and were in hospital. "Some are in shock," an airline source said.

Sheikh Hamdan bin Mubarak al-Nahayan, head of Abu Dhabi's civil aviation authority, said the pilot tried to stop the plane "but it veered off to the right", the official WAM news agency reported. The airport was closed for several hours.
Sheikh Hamdan said "all of the injuries were minor except for one that was moderate".
At Gulf Air headquarters in Manama, the airline said five passengers suffered "minor injuries while evacuating the plane from the chutes".
"Investigations will take about two days to know exactly what happened," a member of the crew said.
The airline is jointly owned by the governments of Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar.
